title: The Race to Defend Kyiv Against Terrifying New Jet-Powered Drones
key_facts: Forces News reports Russia has gone from experimenting with jet-powered attack drones to reportedly producing thousands every month.
Its newer Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones were in use against Ukrainian cities by January.
Ukraine's claimed interception rate against older Shahed drones was around 90%; against the newer threats it has reportedly fallen below 60%.
Drone strikes reportedly rose eightfold between June and August, approaching 3,000.
Ukraine is building jet-powered interceptors; President Zelensky announced in late September that four such systems were entering service.
Satellite imagery shows a new launch site about 250 miles inside Russia, reportedly able to hold 500 jet-powered drones.
quote_evidence: Ukraine's claimed interception rate against older Shahed drones had reached around 90%.
Against the newer threats, that figure has reportedly fallen below 60%.
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced in late September that four such systems were entering service.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster Russian drones are harder to intercept, putting Kyiv's winter air defence under pressure.
